note: The landmark buildings on this map are drawn at EMPHASIS, not to scale. Each one keeps its published footprint, its published position and the year a published register gives it; what is exaggerated is only how large it is drawn, by up to 5.0 times, and only while it would otherwise be too small on screen to recognise. The measured height and area are carried on every record here and are what the page states. See wonder/BLOCK-WONDER.md.

heroes.an: the published footprint that the FAA Digital Obstacle File's obstacle 06-000120 (TOWER, 977 ft above ground, 1,811 ft above sea level) falls inside — the same federal file render/fetch_dims.py cached for the Golden Gate's towers, re-read over the whole city by hero/dof_city.py because its box stopped at 37.78 N and Sutro Tower stands at 37.755
heroes.dr: The three-armed footprint's 64 m extent and the 210.0 m LIDAR median are measured, and the FAA publishes the obstacle at 977 ft above ground in the same place. The tapering triangular mass, the two platform flares and the mast are drawn. THE LEGS ARE NOT DRAWN SEPARATELY: this is an open lattice drawn as solid members, which is what every other building on this map is drawn as, and the three legs the published ring traces are 2 m wide — at the widest camera in the film one of them is under a pixel.
heroes.measured: Footprint 662.0 m2 on 21 published vertices; roof 210.0 m and top 210.0 m above ground; plan radius 0.00 m; roll year 1974.
heroes.hu: the published ring traces three open steel legs 2 m wide, not an enclosing wall: measured, the largest circle that fits inside it anywhere is 8.7 m across against a 64 m published extent, so a vertex test against the ring is a test about a slab and this is not a slab. The reference is the ring's own convex hull, which is derived from the published geometry and not chosen.

heroes.n: Palace of Fine Arts Exhibition Hall
heroes.an: the footprint that DataSF 97yj-54sx Article 10 landmark no. 88 (`Palace Of Fine Arts`) resolves to in this map's own register: base/places.qc carries `bi` 159037 on that row, with the designation bit set. The rotunda beside it is a different footprint (159057) and is the hero `pofa`.
heroes.ys: the same register and the same reasoning the `pofa` record already carries: rzic-39gi gives landmark no. 88 a `yearbuilt` of 0, so the register has no year for it; 1915 is the year of the Panama-Pacific International Exposition the corpus's own `ppie` entry carries, and the roll dates this footprint 1906, which is FLAG_NOYEAR and not a year.
heroes.dr: The crescent is the published footprint and 14.0 m is the published height; both are read out of the shipped record and neither is authored. What is DRAWN is the section, on the shaped-cap rule: a wall set back 0.70 m, a cornice band at the full published ring, and a roof drawn as a segmental arc over the ring's own equivalent half-width (its area / perimeter), truncated flat where the published 14.0 m top stops it. Every roof band stands on a per-vertex bisector inset of the published ring -- the Conservatory of Flowers' own containment rule -- and the deepest inset drawn is the deepest one at which every vertex of the inset ring is still inside the published ring, searched rather than typed. Nothing stands outside the published footprint and nothing above the published top. The colonnade that curves round the lagoon is a separate set of published footprints and is drawn by the fabric, which is what the `pofa` record already says.
heroes.measured: Footprint 12,297.0 m2 on 30 published vertices; roof 14.0 m and top 14.0 m above ground; plan radius 0.00 m; roll year 1906.
